_comment: This is rulesync 16.18.0's CANONICAL schema, not Claude Code's native one. The event key is camelCase `preToolUse` (rulesync maps it to `PreToolUse` on generate), and each definition is FLAT -- matcher/type/command as siblings -- because rulesync builds the nested {matcher, hooks:[{type,command}]} shape itself. The top-level `hooks` record is required by rulesync's Zod schema even though only the claudecode override carries content: every per-tool override block, `claudecode` included, is wrapped in z.optional() and this one is not. BOTH FAILURE MODES BELOW WERE RE-MEASURED ON THE PINNED VERSION. MODE 1 DID NOT MOVE. MODE 2 DID, on the MINOR bump to 16.18.0: generate now EXITS 1 and prints no summary line at all, where every version before it exited 0 under an ordinary All done! line. That settles a question this note used to leave open -- it recorded mode 2 as having held its shape across every version tested, and treated a MAJOR bump as the thing to watch for. A MINOR one moved it. MODE 1, THE NESTED SHAPE. Feed it Claude Code's native PascalCase/nested shape and stderr warns `Skipped hook event(s) for claudecode (not supported): PreToolUse` -- but `Skipped` is the WARNING's word, not the OUTPUT's, and believing it is how this file shipped inert once already. The override block is merged in UNFILTERED (only the shared `hooks` record is filtered to supported events) and an unmapped event name passes through VERBATIM, so `PreToolUse` lands at exactly the path Claude Code reads. There `type` defaults to `command` when absent, and the emitted command is read from the definition's OWN `command` field -- which the nested shape has not got, because the real command sits in an inner `hooks` array rulesync never looks in. What lands is {matcher: Bash, hooks: [{type: command}]}: well-formed, correctly placed, and carrying no command at all. THE COUNT GATE IS BLIND TO THIS ONE -- the full file set is written, the `+ 1 hooks` summary term is present, and guard_rulesync_drift.py exits 0. Only guard_emitted_outputs.py reds, which is the whole reason it reads structure rather than counting. MODE 2, OMITTING THE TOP-LEVEL `hooks` KEY. generate prints a Zod error (`expected record, received undefined` at path `hooks`) and still writes every other output -- CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .claude/agents/, .claude/skills/ -- with .claude/settings.json ALONE not rewritten. On 16.18.0 it EXITS 1 and prints NO `All done!` summary at all; every earlier version measured exited 0 under an ordinary one. Re-measured on this version: the file is PRESENT rather than missing, because it is tracked and the checkout supplies it -- which is exactly why scripts/reset_tracked_hooks.py clears its `hooks` key first. Without that clear, a stale-but-structurally-valid copy survives the failed run and satisfies the emitted-output guard; with it, the un-rewritten key reds both gates. The 'missing' wording here described the era before that file was tracked. The Zod error goes to STDERR and CI pipes only STDOUT into the drift guard, so the error text never reaches it; what reds that guard on 16.18.0 is the `All done!` line being absent ENTIRELY (exit 2, no summary line), where before it was the `+ 1 hooks` term missing from a summary that was present. THREE things catch this one now, and the earliest is new: CI runs `npm run rulesync | tee` under `set -euo pipefail`, so the non-zero exit fails the PIPELINE and the step aborts BEFORE either guard runs -- measured. Both guards still red if reached. A CORRECTION THIS FILE USED TO CARRY, AND THE REASON TO MEASURE ON A FRESH TREE. An earlier note here recorded that under a much older version the same omission wrote nothing at all and printed `All files are up to date`, and called that an inversion in the dangerous direction. IT DOES NOT REPRODUCE. Re-run against that version on a FRESH tree -- under the `-t` list in force when it was pinned as well as today's -- and it behaves exactly as described above: exit 0, every other output written, only settings.json missing, and no `up to date` line anywhere. The likeliest origin is the trap guard_rulesync_drift.py names in its own prose: rulesync SKIPS a file whose content already matches, so a run in an ALREADY-GENERATED tree prints `All files are up to date` whatever the input says. Wipe the outputs first or the measurement is worthless. So the honest record is that mode 2 held its shape across every version tested until 16.18.0, then moved -- in the SAFE direction, louder and earlier. Re-measure on the next bump regardless. The reason outlives the result: MODE 1 still exits 0 under an ordinary summary, and THAT is what makes a change in it invisible; not any history of having moved. WHAT EACH GATE IS FOR. scripts/guard_rulesync_drift.py compares the emitted counts against a pinned map and sees the hooks feature expected but absent -- in mode 2 only. scripts/guard_emitted_outputs.py reads the emitted .claude/settings.json STRUCTURALLY -- it requires a command that RUNS the guard to sit at hooks.PreToolUse[*].hooks[*] with type command, the one path Claude Code executes -- so it fails closed both when the file is absent and when the file looks right but the command is gone. Not a grep: a grep proves only that the string is somewhere in the document, and a command re-nested under another event, carried on a non-command hook, or merely echoed satisfies it while running nothing. AGAINST A HUMAN EDIT, tests/test_hooks_wiring.py pins this shape and this comment is only a courtesy. AGAINST A RULESYNC VERSION BUMP, this comment is the FIRST defence and no longer the only one: the offline suite asserts THIS file, so a rulesync that renamed `preToolUse` or re-nested the definitions would leave it green -- but the emitted-output guard reads the generated ARTIFACT, so it catches the dropped command whatever the input schema was renamed to. Re-verify the emitted .claude/settings.json by hand when changing the pinned version in package.json.
